page.title: Islanders marketing stories
page.description: Three marketing journeys: member campaigns, group-night sales handoffs, and fan-event RSVPs. Follow the creative, content and alternate outcomes.
page.subtitle: Member campaigns, group nights and fan events — from the promotion to the next action.

sections.heading: From member email to guest tickets
sections.text: Follow the steps: system flow, marketing workspace and fan phone stay in sync. Campaign and integrations are illustrative; imagery is from the Islanders' official membership pages. A/B are walkthrough annotations, not fan-facing UI. The 9:41 clock is display-only.

steps.text: **The promotion.** This is the member email from Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The phone shows its actual creative and the campaign link the fan will click.
Click Explore member guest tickets. The member website checks sign-in and membership, then shows the promised guest-access content. Recognition alone is not ticketing authorization.

**Match the content to the page.** The Contentful mockup shows the same official Islanders photo used on the phone. Compare A (headline) and B (button); the destination points to the member ticket offer.
View guest-ticket options leads to the matching Ticketmaster Account Manager offer. Ticketmaster verifies eligibility and supplies inventory and prices; this concept does not simulate checkout.

**Stop the reminder after purchase.** In this simulated outcome, an illustrative integration supplies Ticketmaster's confirmed purchase to Salesforce Marketing Cloud. At the reminder decision, this member matches the Purchased path and exits; a click alone does not qualify.
The same email link opens a sign-in gate when membership is not verified. Preserve the campaign destination so the fan does not have to find the offer again.
After illustrative member verification, return to the original landing page and its guest-ticket CTA. No credentials are collected by this demo.
An old email still points to this campaign, but the offer has ended. Serve the published fallback copy and remove the expired member-offer checkout link.
**Replace the expired promise.** Contentful supplies the fallback headline and button. A and B match the phone; the new destination is regular tickets, with no expired member offer.
The fallback opens regular ticket options. Preserve campaign attribution if appropriate, but carry no expired member entitlement into ticketing.

sections.heading: From group invitation to useful sales handoff
sections.text: Proposed journey, not the Islanders’ deployed stack. Official team imagery; illustrative campaign, records and integrations. Focused app mockups, not account screenshots. A/B mark source-to-screen matches. Clock is illustrative staging.

steps.text: **Start with the invitation.** The fan sees the group-night email; Content Builder shows the same creative, button and campaign destination. This is a proposed campaign, not a live offer.
**Follow the promise.** Plan your group night opens this campaign landing page—not a generic homepage. The two choices let the organizer ask for planning help or explore ticket options.

**Check the source against the screen.** Contentful holds the same official group photo and A headline shown on the phone. B is the planning CTA. These custom fields and their website mapping are proposed.

**Ask for useful context.** The example organizer requests planning help for 24 people and hospitality. This is still a form, not a lead or a booking. Routing follows the request type, not an invented group-size threshold.

**Submit the planning request.** In this proposed handoff, Sales Cloud receives the campaign, group size and preferences. Compare the phone acknowledgement with the lead record: inquiry received does not mean seats reserved.
**Give sales a useful next action.** The lead is still open and not contacted. The proposed task is to discuss hospitality and game preferences; no quote, reservation or response deadline is implied.
**Take the other path.** This fan chooses Tickets only. The proposed campaign route does not create a planning inquiry just because someone clicked a link.

**Hand off to ticketing.** A configured Ticketmaster destination would own availability and checkout. This preview stops at the handoff: no group discount, inventory, payment or purchase is simulated.

sections.heading: From fan invitation to the right confirmation
sections.text: Proposed journey, not the Islanders’ deployed stack. Official team imagery; illustrative campaign, records and integrations. Focused app mockups, not account screenshots. A/B mark source-to-screen matches. Clock is illustrative staging.

steps.text: **Show the invitation.** A proposed fan-social campaign uses official Islanders imagery with an explicitly fictional partner. The email’s Reserve my place button leads to event details—not directly to a confirmed reservation.
**Open the event details.** The fan sees the proposed creative, partner placement and RSVP action. No real date, venue or event is being advertised; this is a walkthrough for reviewing the journey.
**Match the creative to its source.** A is the event headline; B is the RSVP button. Contentful’s proposed custom fields line up with the phone, including the example partner credit.

**Make permission a separate choice.** On the available-capacity path, the fan chooses the optional sponsor checkbox. The Eventbrite-style order form is a focused mockup; custom questions can be optional.

**Confirm only a completed registration.** In this simulated outcome the RSVP succeeded. The organizer record shows Registered and sponsor opt-in Yes as separate values. A click on the invitation did not establish either fact.

**Use the confirmed facts.** The proposed integration passes registration and the separate opt-in answer to Marketing Cloud. The fan receives the reservation message; the sponsor audience includes only explicit opt-ins. No sponsor message is sent in this story.

**Leave sponsor opt-in unchecked.** The same optional question stays unanswered/No. The fan can still finish the RSVP. Declining partner marketing must not change the availability or reservation decision in this proposed journey.

**The place is still reserved.** This simulated registration is successful with sponsor opt-in No. Compare the two fields; the fan’s confirmation must not imply that a sponsor subscription was required.

**Send the event message, not sponsor marketing.** The proposed integration carries Registered plus opt-in No. The reservation confirmation still goes out; the fan is excluded from the proposed sponsor audience.
**Capacity changes the action.** Eventbrite supports a waitlist when the configured ticket type or event is full. The fan now sees Join waitlist, not Reserve my place. No place is held at this step.

**A waitlist is not a ticket.** The simulated fan joins the waitlist and sees an honest acknowledgement. Sponsor permission is not collected on this path; no automatic ticket release or reservation is shown.

**Keep follow-up consistent.** The proposed integration carries Waitlisted, not Registered, with sponsor permission Not collected. The fan receives a waitlist message and is excluded from the proposed sponsor audience.
